Team — thanks for the sync this morning. Two exec asks landed (from Claire / DB): 1) we need a single committed scope for the QBR demo that tolerates the outstanding roadmap exceptions; 2) an ask to confirm fall‑back model variants and latency SLO for the Acme PoC.

I pulled the notes into a table (attached: roadmap-exceptions-sheet.xlsx) and sketched a mutual action plan (attached: mutual_action_plan_acme.xlsx). Requesting owners and dates so I can roll these into the QBR playbook before Friday.

Quick asks:
- Vanessa: confirm which exceptions we can close vs which need exec signoff (status + brief reason).
- Karthik: can you confirm the fallback model variants and estimated p95 serving latency for the demo (approx numbers are fine)?
- Marissa: procurement path — are we on track for the contract amendments Acme asked for? (I cc'd Dara to keep Acme in the loop.)

I'll consolidate replies into the playbook and surface a short decision register for exec review. If anyone wants a quick 15 to align, ping me.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake

- Exceptions needing exec signoff: the cross‑region KV eviction policy and customer‑facing SLA wording. Need legal + Claire to sign.

Thanks — quick tech note on fallback model variants for demo:

Option A (preferred): quantized Llama‑2‑13B (FP16 -> int8 friendly) — expected p95 generation latency (demo setup): ~220ms/token on dedicated T4 pool, throughput comfortably supports demo scale.
Option B (cost‑saver): 7B distilled variant — p95 ~160ms/token but lower output fidelity for certain prompts (we should include a short quality checklist).
Option C (safety fallback): hosted Redwood‑tiny variant — deterministic, latency ~85ms/token but cannot run the long‑context retrieval flow.

I'll add these to the mutual_action_plan_acme.xlsx with recommended fallback order and a short risk note. Also, Vivek — we should confirm the routing policy to prefer dedicated for the demo window; I left a note in the Drive link.

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer
